sources.entry: Syncloud - OS with an app store and automatic updates for apps such as Nextcloud, Jellyfin, Bitwarden and Paperless, including HTTPS, a domain name and remote access without a public IP. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Go/Shell

summary.one_liner: Syncloud is a self-hosting OS image or pre-built device for running popular apps with a built-in app store, HTTPS, domain name, and remote access.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Syncloud as a simple way to self-host popular apps, distributed as an image or a pre-built device. The image contains a Debian-based Linux OS, a Snap-based app installer, and a platform snap package that provides shared services to all apps and manages device settings. The README covers web UI development with Node.js (npm run dev:stub) and building a platform snap package locally using the Drone CLI. It also shows how to install a snap package on a device with snap install --devmode. The README itself does not detail specific apps or features; the app store, HTTPS, domain name and remote access details come from the awesome-selfhosted listing description.
use_cases: self-host personal apps on a home device
run Nextcloud or Jellyfin without manual server setup
remote access to home services without a public IP
install self-hosted apps from an app store
build a platform snap package for development
how_to_run: Download an image for your device from the project's download page (see README)
notable: Ships as a complete OS image or pre-built device rather than a single app
Snap-based app installer for installing apps
Platform snap package provides shared services and device settings for all apps
Drone-based build pipeline for amd64, arm64 and arm targets
caveats: README is brief and gives little detail on features or supported hardware
Local package builds rely on the Drone CLI and a trusted exec pipeline
Installing a snap requires --devmode, which bypasses normal snap confinement
